newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti shares suspended up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti shares suspended up 10 pct.

text.p: Shares in Italian information technology group Olivetti rose 10 percent shortly after the stock market opening on Wednesday, triggering an automatic suspension to their trade on the bourse, dealers said.
Shares had begun 7.44 percent higher at 780 lire per share earlier before being suspended at 798 lire shortly after 0810 GMT.
Olivetti stock rose sharply at the start following news that chairman Carlo De Benedetti had resigned from his post and from the loss-making group's board late on Tuesday.

Olivetti shares had fallen around nine percent, close to all-time lows, on Monday and Tuesday as rumours abounded in the stock market about conflict between top managers and on concern about the company's financial health.

Under an automatic suspension, a stock is suspended for a set period and resumes trading if there are price quotes below the 10 percent ceiling. Dealers said the share is expected to resume at 0843 GMT.
Alternatively stock market authorities can decide to widen the trading bands.
